rules.comment: Surviving wife with descendants takes 1/8 (faraïd). The residuary (asaba) is split among sons and daughters with the doctrinal 2:1 ratio (sons : daughters). Article numbers reflect the canonical Moudawana Livre VI; the snippet is empty because the dev PDF is a stub.

Surviving wife without descendants takes 1/4 (faraïd). The residuary then flows to the remaining qualifying heirs per the Livre VI hierarchy — NOT modelled here because the engine does not yet codify ascendants/collaterals.
Surviving husband with descendants takes 1/4 (faraïd). The wizard currently only models a single spouse slot; this rule documents the doctrinal asymmetry between husband and wife shares.
Surviving husband without descendants takes 1/2 (faraïd). Same modelling caveat as the previous rule.
Mother takes 1/6 in the presence of descendants. Modelled as a fixed share; ascendants are not yet a wizard input.
Father takes 1/6 in the presence of male descendants. With only female descendants the father is also asaba on the residuary — not modelled in this draft.
Two or more daughters with no sons share 2/3 collectively. A single daughter without sons takes 1/2 — separate rule needed if the wizard distinguishes the count.
A single daughter without sons takes 1/2 (faraïd).

non_modelled_concepts: hajb (exclusion of an heir by a closer-degree heir)
'awl (proportional reduction when fixed shares exceed unity)
radd (devolution of the residue when no asaba is present)
asaba ordering across degrees (paternal grandfather, brothers, etc.)
interaction with EU 650/2012 applicable-law selection (handled by a separate skeleton iter, not here)
